## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

The controller package: how an instructor drives the simulation — the hidden same-screen panel, a phone or tablet
remote, a second-screen viewer, the scenario runner and the relay that joins devices in a classroom. One device, the
host, owns the engine; the others send commands and receive events and low-rate state, never raw waveform samples. A
clinician-educator can see what the panel and scenarios can do; an embedding developer gets the wire protocol and the
transports (`src/protocol.ts`).
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- Host authority: commands in → dispatch → acknowledgement; engine events out, batched per frame; a `state` event at
  1 Hz; a snapshot for every peer that says hello (`src/session/host-session.ts`, `src/protocol.ts`).
- No samples on the wire: the message types have no field that can hold one, and the guard refuses binary data, long
  numeric runs, waveform keys and oversized or deeply nested messages (`src/guard.ts`).
- A viewer runs its own engine from the host's snapshot, mirrors each applied command at the host's tick and follows the
  host's 1 Hz anchors a fixed wall-time delay behind; the deterministic engine makes it sample-identical on the same
  build, and it resyncs by saying hello again (`src/session/viewer-sync.ts`).
- The scenario runner is a pure state machine: timers accumulate sim time while the scenario is not paused, each vital
  condition has its own "continuously true for" counter, and the interval is credited with the values held before the
  call, so the result does not depend on how often it is called (`src/scenario/runner.ts`; research 01 §2.3).
- Transitions are tried in document order and the first that holds fires, at most one per call; a probability is one
  draw on the `scenario` random stream (`src/scenario/runner.ts`). The same seed and log reproduce every state entry
  and draw (`src/scenario/replay.ts`).
- Staged commands are sent with one stage group and applied by the host on one tick (`src/panel/staging.ts`;
  research 01 §4).
- The relay keeps rooms keyed by a 6-character session code, routes by host authority, caches a snapshot for late
  joiners, keeps a heartbeat and expires rooms (`relay/server.ts`).
- Reconnect delay = min(max, base·2^attempt) × (1 ± jitter), by default 250 ms, 8 s and 20 % (`src/transport/backoff.ts`
  [ENG]).
- The panel and remote generate their controls from the engine's vocabulary of bounds, normals and enums
  (`src/vocabulary.ts`; research 04 §5).
<!-- /hand:equations -->
